items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Irv Cottler, who played drums with Frank Sinatra for 20 years.

ctx.x: What prompted you to move from one coast to the other?

Well I got burned out to start with. I was married to a lady and we got divorced. Because I met her in California and we got married. I was 24, she was about 18. I moved to California, and I’d leave her here. I lived in New York, I’d leave her here, and I’d go on the road for eight, nine months at a time. And we had no life. I mean I was bad. I was really bad in those days. And so we got divorced and about six months later we started talking again, you know, saying if I would stay home more maybe we could work it…

Frank Sinatra for 20 years. “Are you kidding? Forget about it. Goodbye.” He hung up on me. I got a call about three days later. And then he said, “Listen, I’m going to put you on staff.” And I knew the reason why. The reason why was because I used to do these television — like Dinah Shore Show — as a guest. Now they don’t have to pay me because they can put me on these shows. So he was going to put me on. So in the long run NBC would save money. items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I was going to start out with the Charlie Parker, Benny Goodman, Steve Allen, Frank Sinatra.

ctx.x: Wow. And am I correct that when you were — the band was super popular yet the scale was $15 and you were lucky to make $11?

Well after the scale was 19 but I gave the band boy $8 and I made 11. And I was never happier in my whole life. You know what? I read — I didn’t start a band, it was a record date that started the band. I think — without having to explain the whole thing — I always tell people that I’m not trying to sell books because the book has been out since 2004, and I don’t get much money, if I ever did get much money from the book, I never wrote a book to make money.
